blocks.text: After breakfast, a full-day city tour of Quito and the Equator Line (about 8 hours). Founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca city, at about 2,850 m, Quito keeps one of the best-preserved historic centres in Latin America, a showcase of the Quito School of Art, and was among the very first places inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List. On foot through the Old Town: the neo-Gothic Basílica del Voto Nacional, with gargoyles shaped like iguanas, turtles and boobies, San Francisco church and square, the Plaza Grande with the Cathedral, the Presidential Palace and City Hall, and the Jesuit church of La Compañía, with its carved façade and golden interior; then the view from El Panecillo, crowned by the Winged Virgin of Quito. In the afternoon, the Middle of the World: the Ciudad Mitad del Mundo, whose 30-metre monument commemorates the French Geodesic Mission of 1736 (GPS later placed the true equator about 240 m away), and the Intiñán Museum, with experiments on the equator and displays on ancient Ecuadorian cultures. Overnight at Hotel Finlandia 4★. (B)

blocks.text: After breakfast, a full day (about 11 hours) via the Cotopaxi valley, visiting a rose plantation (closed at weekends and on public holidays). Continue on a scenic drive to Quilotoa, stopping at a Tigua art workshop, with its colourful paintings of Andean life. At the Quilotoa crater, admire the emerald-green lake inside the volcano, ringed by steep, jagged cliffs: a viewpoint and a walk through the nearby Indigenous community; hiking down to the lake, kayaking and mule rides are optional, not included, and offered by locals until about 15:00. Continue to Baños (about 3.5 hours). Overnight at Hotel La Floresta 3★. (B)

blocks.text: Baños, at about 1,800 m in a lush valley at the foot of Tungurahua Volcano (about 5,020 m), is known for its waterfalls, hot springs and outdoor activities. After a walk through the town centre, follow the Route of the Waterfalls: Agoyán, the Manto de la Novia (Bride’s Veil, with an optional cable car) and the spectacular Pailón del Diablo (Devil’s Cauldron); try the “Swing at the End of the World” or zip-line over the Pastaza Canyon (optional, USD 15). Free afternoon, with optional thermal baths. Overnight at Hotel La Floresta 3★. (B)
